subjects.name: English
examTips: Vocabulary = 6-8 Qs: Synonyms, Antonyms, One-word. Memorize 300 high-frequency FPSC words
Prepositions are guaranteed traps: good AT, interested IN, fond OF, similar TO, capable OF
Tense marker method: since/for -> perfect continuous, yesterday -> past simple
BS-17 includes Vocabulary section, BS-16 syllabus says only Grammar + Sentence Structuring but still expect 4-5 vocabulary
Negative marking: don't guess vocabulary if unsure

keyPoints: Benevolent = kind-hearted, Verbose = wordy, Concise = brief (antonym of verbose)
Ambiguous = more than one meaning, Lucid = clear, Mitigate = lessen
Ephemeral = short-lived, Ubiquitous = present everywhere, Altruism = selflessness
One-word: Insolvent = cannot pay debts, Hermit = lives alone, Philanthropist = loves mankind
Spelling FPSC traps: Accommodation, Occurrence, Privilege, Embarrassment, Liaison
Neither/Either/Each/Every + singular verb: Neither of the students HAS done
Active to Passive: Present Continuous 'is checking' -> 'are being checked'
Direct to Indirect: 'today'->'that day', 'tomorrow'->'next day', 'here'->'there'
Articles: 'an hour', 'a university' (sound based), 'the' for superlatives
Prepositions: Good AT (skill), Good IN (behaviour), Angry AT (thing), Angry WITH (person)
formulas: Present Perfect Continuous: has/have been + V-ing + since/for

keyPoints: Sentence types: Simple, Compound (FANBOYS), Complex (subordinate clause)
Common correction: 'The committee has submitted its report' not 'their'
Dangling modifier: 'Walking through forest, snake bit him' is wrong
Parallelism: 'He likes reading, writing and to swim' -> 'swimming'
Layers: Troposphere (0-8-18km, temp decreases), Stratosphere (ozone max 20-50km, temp increases), Mesosphere (temp decreases to -90C), Thermosphere (temp increases, aurora), Exosphere
Tropopause height: ~17km equator, ~8km poles. Coldest point
Ozone layer: 20-50km, max concentration at 25km, Dobson unit
fpsc_traps: Troposphere contains 75% mass, Stratosphere contains ozone, not Troposphere

keyPoints: Ideal gas: p = ρ R_d T, R_d = 287 J/kg/K, R_v = 461
Hydrostatic: dp = -ρ g dz => pressure decreases exponentially
First law: dQ = c_v dT + p dα, dry adiabatic process dQ=0
DALR = g/c_p = 9.8°C/km, SALR ~6°C/km (variable due to latent heat)
Potential temperature θ = T*(1000/p)^(R/c_p) conserved for dry adiabatic
Stability: If ELR < DALR stable, ELR > DALR unstable, saturated uses SALR
mustRemember: Latent heat release makes SALR less than DALR

keyPoints: Solar constant ~1361 W/m2, Albedo Earth ~0.30
Stefan-Boltzmann: E = σT^4, Wien's law λmax = 2897/T
Scattering: Rayleigh (λ^-4, blue sky), Mie (white clouds), Non-selective
Humidity: Mixing ratio w = 0.622 e/(p-e), Relative humidity RH = e/e_s *100
Clausius-Clapeyron: e_s increases ~7% per degree warming
Psychrometer: dry & wet bulb, depression gives humidity
Cloud classification: Low (St, Sc, Ns <2km), Middle (Ac, As 2-7km), High (Ci, Cs, Cc 5-13km), Vertical (Cu, Cb)
Formation: Convection, Orographic, Frontal, Convergence
Precipitation: Bergeron process (ice crystals grow at expense of droplets), Collision-coalescence (warm rain)
Types: Drizzle, Rain, Snow, Sleet, Hail, Graupel
fpsc_traps: Cumulonimbus = thunderstorm cloud, Nimbostratus = continuous rain

keyPoints: Geostrophic wind: Balance pressure gradient & Coriolis, Vg = (1/fρ) * Δp/Δn, parallel to isobars
Gradient wind: adds centrifugal for curved flow
Thermal wind: vertical shear of geostrophic wind due to horizontal temp gradient
Local winds: Sea breeze (day sea->land), Land breeze (night), Mountain-valley, Foehn/Chinook (warm dry downslope), Loo in Pakistan
Jet streams: Subtropical (STJ) & Polar (PFJ), core speed 100-200 knots, at 200-300 hPa
pakistanContext: Monsoon low, Heat low over Balochistan drives monsoon

keyPoints: Air masses: cP, cA, mP, mT, cT - Pakistan affected by cP in winter (Western Disturbances), mT from Arabian Sea in summer
Fronts: Cold (steep, heavy rain), Warm (gentle slope, prolonged), Occluded, Stationary
Extra-tropical cyclone: Formation along polar front, Norwegian model, life cycle 3-7 days
Tropical cyclone: Requires SST >26.5C, Coriolis, low shear, formation 5-20° latitude. Eye, eyewall, spiral bands. Pakistan: Arabian Sea cyclones (Tauktae, Biparjoy)
Thunderstorm: 3 stages Cu, Mature, Dissipating. Conditions: instability, moisture, lift. Types: single, multi-cell, super-cell
mustRemember: Pakistan monsoon depressions form in Bay of Bengal, move NW to Pakistan

keyPoints: Instruments: Barometer (aneroid/mercury), Anemometer, Wind vane, Hygrometer, Sunshine recorder, Radiosonde (PTU + GPS)
Charts: Surface chart (isobars, fronts), 850hPa (monsoon), 500hPa (troughs), 200hPa (jet)
METAR, SYNOP codes: QNH, visibility, cloud cover in oktas
Forecasting: Synoptic, Statistical, Persistence, NWP (initialization, data assimilation, models: GFS, ECMWF, ICON)
Satellite: INSAT, Meteosat, Himawari. Channels: VIS (albedo), IR (temp), WV (moisture). Radar: dBZ reflectivity, Doppler velocity
PMD models: WRF, used for 3-day forecast
Controls: Latitude, Altitude, Continentality, Ocean currents, Prevailing winds, Topography
Koppen: A Tropical, B Dry, C Temperate, D Cold, E Polar. Subtypes: f=fully humid, m=monsoon, w=winter dry, s=summer dry. Pakistan: BWh (hot desert), BWk, Cwa
Thornthwaite based on precipitation effectiveness & thermal efficiency
World: Equatorial (Af), Monsoon (Am), Savanna (Aw), Desert (BWh), Steppe (BSh), Mediterranean (Csa), etc.
Pakistan: 4 seasons - Winter (Dec-Feb) WD rain, Pre-monsoon (Apr-Jun) hot/dusty, Monsoon (Jul-Sep) 60% rain, Post-monsoon (Oct-Nov)
Monsoon mechanism: Land-sea thermal contrast, ITCZ shift to 25N, Somali Jet, Tibetan High, Heat low over Balochistan
Onset: Karachi early July, Islamabad early July, retreat September
Western Disturbances: Originate Mediterranean, 4-6 per month in winter, cause rain/snow in north, fog in plains
Temperature extremes: Jacobabad/Sibi up to 53C, Skardu -25C
pakistanContext: 2022 floods due to +60% monsoon + glacier melt, 2010 super flood due to WD + monsoon interaction

keyPoints: ENSO: El Nino (warm central Pacific, weak monsoon Pakistan often), La Nina (cold, strong monsoon, 2020-2022 La Nina contributed to floods)
IOD: Positive IOD (warm west Indian Ocean) enhances monsoon, Negative suppresses
Global warming: 1.1C since pre-industrial, Pakistan warming 0.3C/decade, glaciers melting
IPCC AR6: Human influence unequivocal, 1.5C threshold around 2030s
Paleoclimate: Ice cores, Dendrochronology, Milankovitch cycles (eccentricity 100k, obliquity 41k, precession 23k years)
Newton: F=ma, Law of gravitation F=Gm1m2/r^2
Work-energy: KE=0.5mv^2, PE=mgh, Escape velocity Ve=√(2gR)=11.2km/s
Bernoulli: p + 0.5ρv^2 + ρgh = constant - explains lift, venturi
Viscosity: Newton's law τ=μ dv/dy, Reynolds number Re=ρvL/μ, laminar if <2000
Laws: 0th (thermal equilibrium), 1st (dU=dQ-dW), 2nd (entropy increases), 3rd (0K unattainable)
Kinetic theory: PV=(1/3)mN c^2, RMS speed = √(3RT/M)
Specific heats: Cp-Cv=R, γ=Cp/Cv=1.4 for diatomic
Blackbody radiation important for meteorology
Wave: v=fλ, Sound speed in air ~343 m/s, increases with temperature
Doppler: f' = f (v±vo)/(v±vs) - used in radar
Optics: Snell's law n1 sinθ1=n2 sinθ2, Total internal reflection for mirage
Scattering: Rayleigh ∝1/λ^4 explains blue sky, red sunset
EM spectrum: Radio>Microwave>IR>Visible>UV>Xray>Gamma, all speed c=3e8 m/s
Quadratic: ax^2+bx+c=0, roots = (-b±√(b^2-4ac))/2a, discriminant D=b^2-4ac
Matrices: Determinant, Inverse exists if det≠0
Calculus: d/dx x^n = n x^(n-1), ∫x^n dx = x^(n+1)/(n+1). d/dx sinx=cosx, e^x=e^x
Differential eq: First order separable, used for growth/decay, Newton's cooling
Vectors: Dot a·b=|a||b|cosθ, Cross |a×b|=|a||b|sinθ
Mean = sum/n, Median middle value, Mode most frequent
Variance = Σ(x-mean)^2/n, SD = sqrt(variance), SD measures spread
Correlation r: -1 to +1, r>0.7 strong positive, Regression y=a+bx
Probability: P(A and B)=P(A)*P(B) if independent, Normal distribution 68-95-99.7 rule
For meteorological data: Anomaly = observed - climatological mean
mustRemember: Standard deviation of weather data indicates variability, used in climate normals (30-year mean 1991-2020)

keyPoints: Air pollutants: PM2.5 (<2.5 micron most dangerous), NOx, SO2, CO, O3. AQI categories 0-50 Good to 300+ Hazardous. Lahore often 200+ in winter
Smog = Smoke+Fog, photochemical smog needs sunlight + NOx + VOCs
Acid rain: pH<5.6, due to SO2+NOx -> H2SO4+HNO3, damages crops
Ozone depletion: CFCs release Cl, one Cl destroys 100k O3, Montreal Protocol 1987 success
Greenhouse gases: CO2 (76%), CH4 (16%, 80x more potent 20yr), N2O, HFCs. CO2 420ppm now vs 280 pre-industrial
pakistanContext: Pakistan 5th most vulnerable to climate change (Germanwatch), 2022 floods damage $30bn

keyPoints: Ecosystem: Producers->Primary consumers->Secondary, 10% energy transfer
Biodiversity hotspots: Pakistan has Himalaya hotspot
Conventions: UNFCCC 1992, Kyoto 1997 (binding for developed), Paris 2015 (limit to <2C, aim 1.5C, NDCs)
Pakistan policies: National Climate Change Policy 2021, PEPA 1997, Ten Billion Tree Tsunami
Renewable: Solar potential Balochistan, Wind corridor Gharo-Jhimpir 50GW potential
Research types: Descriptive, Analytical, Experimental, Exploratory
Sampling: Random, Stratified (best for heterogeneous like Pakistan provinces), Cluster, Systematic
Data types: Nominal (names), Ordinal (rank), Interval (temp C), Ratio (Kelvin, has true zero)
Hypothesis testing: Null H0 (no effect), Alternate H1. p<0.05 significant => reject H0
Errors: Type I (false positive, α), Type II (false negative, β). Confidence interval 95% means 95% contains true value
Correlation vs Causation: Correlation doesn't imply causation, spurious correlation example ice-cream & drowning
Time series: Trend, Seasonality, Noise. Moving average smooths, Anomaly detection
Earth interior: Crust (5-70km), Mantle (2900km), Outer core liquid, Inner core solid
Plate tectonics: 7 major plates, 3 boundaries: Convergent (Himalaya, earthquakes), Divergent (Mid-Atlantic), Transform (San Andreas)
Faults: Normal (extension), Reverse (compression), Strike-slip (shear). Pakistan: Chaman Fault (strike-slip), Main Boundary Thrust
Waves: P (primary, longitudinal, 6km/s, through solid+liquid), S (secondary, transverse, 3.5km/s, only solid, more destructive), Surface: Love & Rayleigh (slow, most destructive, cause shaking)
Shadow zones: P wave 103-143°, S wave 103° onwards (proves liquid outer core)
Focus = underground origin, Epicenter = point above focus on surface
Magnitude: Richter (log10 amplitude, local), Moment Magnitude Mw = (2/3)log10(M0)-10.7 (more accurate, no saturation, used by USGS). Each +1 = 32x energy
Intensity: Mercalli scale I-XII based on damage & perception, depends on distance, geology
Seismograph: Inertial mass + spring, records velocity/displacement, modern broadband
Pakistan zones: Zone 1 (low), 2A, 2B, 3 (high), 4 (very high). Islamabad in 2B, Quetta, Gwadar in 4, Karachi 2B
Major events: 2005 Kashmir Mw7.6, 2013 Awaran Mw7.7, 1935 Quetta Mw7.7, 1945 Makran tsunami Mw8.1
pakistanContext: PMD seismic network 35 stations, National Seismic Monitoring Center Islamabad

keyPoints: Minerals: Hardness Mohs 1-10 (Talc to Diamond), Luster, Cleavage, Streak. Quartz, Feldspar most common
Rocks: Igneous (Granite intrusive, Basalt extrusive), Sedimentary (Sandstone, Limestone, Shale - stratified, fossils), Metamorphic (Marble from limestone, Slate from shale, Gneiss)
Rock cycle: Igneous -> weathering -> sedimentary -> metamorphism -> melting

Geological Time: Hadean (4.6-4Ga), Archean, Proterozoic, Phanerozoic (Paleozoic, Mesozoic - age of dinosaurs, Cenozoic - current). Quaternary (2.6Ma-present) includes Holocene (11.7kya-present, human civilization)
Structures: Anticline (upward fold, oil trap), Syncline (down), Faults, Unconformity (gap in record)
Geomorphology: Weathering (physical/chemical), Erosion by river (V-shaped valley), Glacier (U-shaped), Wind (yardangs in Balochistan)
Hydrogeology: Aquifer (permeable), Aquitard, Water table, Artesian well. Indus alluvial aquifer major water source
Pakistan: 3 main domains: Indian Plate (Punjab, Sindh sedimentary), Kohistan-Ladakh arc, Eurasian Plate. Salt Range (Pre-Cambrian salt), Sulaiman-Kirthar, Himalayan thrust belts
Economic: Thar coal, Saindak copper-gold, Reko Diq, Sui gas field
